chapter: Class 11 Ch 8 - Cell: The Unit of Life

claims.text: The cell is the fundamental structural and functional unit of all living organisms.

scenes.narration: Every living thing is built from cells. The cell is the fundamental structural and functional unit of all living organisms.

checkpoint.stem: Which statement best describes a cell?
options: A tissue made of many organs
The fundamental structural and functional unit of living organisms
A structure found only in animals
The largest part of a plant
explanations: Incorrect: tissues are made of cells, not the reverse.
Correct: the cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life.
Incorrect: plants, fungi and bacteria also have cells.
Incorrect: cells are the basic unit, not a plant part.
checkpoint.remediation: Revisit: all organisms are composed of cells.

scenes.objective: Trace the development of cell theory.

claims.text: Schleiden (1838) studied plants and Schwann (1839) studied animal cells.
Virchow (1855) explained that new cells form from pre-existing cells.

scenes.narration: In 1838 Schleiden found that plants are made of cells. In 1839 Schwann studied animal cells. In 1855 Virchow explained that new cells form from pre-existing cells.

checkpoint.stem: Who explained that new cells are formed from pre-existing cells?
explanations: Incorrect: Schleiden studied plant cells.
Incorrect: Schwann studied animal cells.
Correct: Virchow (1855) explained cell division gives new cells.
Incorrect: Robert Brown discovered the nucleus.

scenes.objective: Know the two points of modern cell theory.

claims.text: All living organisms are composed of cells and products of cells.
All cells arise from pre-existing cells.

scenes.narration: Cell theory as understood today has two points. All living organisms are composed of cells and products of cells. And all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

checkpoint.stem: Which is NOT part of cell theory as understood today?
options: All organisms are composed of cells and products of cells
All cells arise from pre-existing cells
Cells form de novo from non-living matter
Cells are the unit of living organisms
explanations: Part of the theory.
Part of the theory.
Correct: cells arise from pre-existing cells, not from abiotic matter.
Consistent with the theory.
checkpoint.remediation: Revisit the two points of cell theory.

scenes.objective: Distinguish prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells by the nucleus.

claims.text: Eukaryotic cells have a membrane bound nucleus; prokaryotic cells lack one.
Prokaryotic genetic material is naked, not enveloped by a nuclear membrane.

scenes.narration: Cells with a membrane bound nucleus are eukaryotic. Cells that lack one are prokaryotic, where the genetic material is naked and not enveloped by a nuclear membrane.

checkpoint.stem: A cell has no membrane bound nucleus. It is most likely:
explanations: Incorrect: eukaryotes have a membrane bound nucleus.
Correct: prokaryotes lack a membrane bound nucleus.
Incorrect: plant cells are eukaryotic.
Incorrect: animal cells are eukaryotic.

scenes.objective: Recall organelle differences and what both cell types share.

claims.text: Eukaryotic cells have membrane bound organelles; prokaryotic cells lack them.
Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found in all cells.

scenes.narration: Eukaryotic cells have membrane bound organelles that compartmentalise the cytoplasm. Prokaryotic cells lack them. Ribosomes are found in all cells, and are not membrane bound.

checkpoint.stem: Which structure is found in BOTH prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
explanations: Incorrect: mitochondria are membrane bound organelles of eukaryotes.
Incorrect: Golgi is a membrane bound organelle.
Correct: ribosomes occur in all cells.
Incorrect: ER is a membrane bound organelle.

claims.text: Plant cells have cell walls, plastids and a large central vacuole, absent in animal cells.

scenes.narration: Plant and animal cells differ. Plant cells possess cell walls, plastids and a large central vacuole, which are absent in animal cells.

checkpoint.stem: Which is present in plant cells but absent in animal cells?
explanations: Incorrect: both have a plasma membrane.
Incorrect: both have ribosomes.
Incorrect: both are eukaryotic with a nucleus.
Correct: cell wall, plastids and a large central vacuole are plant features.
